overall_summary: Deduplication and recency weighting across hourly observations reveal that 'What If' scenarios and extreme space anomalies published within the last 7 days (such as IYuce8vaU3Y, YlDuGu1vzAg, and 8KEl0_pJ_68) dominate views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view up to ~0.037). Conversely, standard explanatory facts or older psychological/animal trivia from 3+ weeks ago exhibit heavily stagnated daily velocity. High-performing hooks heavily rely on immersive second-person hypothetical framing ('What If You Fell Into...') combined with extreme visual environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) generated over 800-1,000+ views rapidly with high like ratios (38 likes on IYuce8vaU3Y).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on immersive, high-stakes hypothetical space scenarios putting the viewer directly inside extreme astrophysical anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: QXuqYERlqSo ('This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!') and v1rrcZLdp4U ('The Planet Darker Than Coal') consistently out-perform standard educational facts by capturing high initial curiosity.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more deep-dive Shorts on bizarre exoplanet weather conditions and ultra-rare material phenomena.

weak_patterns.pattern: Stagnant Older Psychological Tricks & Basic Animal Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Older uploads like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A) and 'The Real Reason Songs Get Stuck In Your Head' (Jc04LVKNd2s) plateaued under 20-50 views after their initial 7-day windows.
